title: Variable Naming Rules - What's Valid?
description: Master variable naming conventions and understand what Robot Framework accepts.

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "Not all variable names are equal. Let me show you what Robot Framework accepts—and what it doesn't. This knowledge prevents cryptic errors."
story.context: Understanding naming rules is crucial. Invalid names cause parse errors. Variables have the same flexibility as keywords—case-insensitive and spacing-flexible. Even spaces are allowed in names—unusual but valid.
story.success: MENTOR-9: "Interesting, right? Both variable NAMES and KEYWORDS are flexible—case and spacing don't matter. Robot Framework normalizes them all. Now you know the rules. Use them wisely."

Log all five variables to demonstrate they work
Add a comment: # Note: ${my-var} would be INVALID (hyphens not allowed)

hints: Spaces in variable names work but are unconventional

theory.title: Variable Naming: Rules, Flexibility, and Best Practices
theory.content:
MENTOR-9 pulls up a diagnostics panel showing parse errors.

"PROTO-7, see these errors? Invalid variable name '${my-var}'. Naming rules prevent this. Let me teach you what works and what doesn't."

Valid Variable Names

Naming StyleExampleValid?
Underscores ${my_var}, ${ship_name} ✅ Yes
Camel case ${myVar}, ${shipName} ✅ Yes
All caps ${MY_VAR}, ${SHIP_NAME} ✅ Yes
Spaces ${my var}, ${ship name} ✅ Yes (unusual)
Numbers (not at start) ${var1}, ${test123} ✅ Yes
Hyphens ${my-var}, ${ship-name} ❌ NO
Starting with number ${1var}, ${123test} ❌ NO
Dots (special meaning) ${my.var} ❌ NO (dict access)

Examples of Valid Names

*** Test Cases ***
Valid Names
    ${username}       Set Variable    admin
    ${user_name}      Set Variable    admin
    ${userName}       Set Variable    admin
    ${UserName}       Set Variable    admin
    ${USERNAME}       Set Variable    admin
    ${user name}      Set Variable    admin    # Spaces OK but unusual
    ${user123}        Set Variable    admin
    ${_private}       Set Variable    admin    # Leading underscore OK

Invalid Names (Will Cause Errors)

*** Test Cases ***
Invalid Names
    ${user-name}      Set Variable    admin    # ❌ Hyphens not allowed
    ${123user}        Set Variable    admin    # ❌ Can't start with number
    ${my.var}         Set Variable    admin    # ❌ Dot has special meaning
    ${user@name}      Set Variable    admin    # ❌ Special chars not allowed
    ${user#name}      Set Variable    admin    # ❌ Hash not allowed

Variable Flexibility: Just Like Keywords!

IMPORTANT: Just like keywords, variable names are CASE-INSENSITIVE AND SPACING-FLEXIBLE!

*** Test Cases ***
Variable Flexibility Test
    ${myVar}    Set Variable    test value
    
    Log    ${myVar}     # Output: "test value"
    Log    ${MyVar}     # Output: "test value" (SAME variable!)
    Log    ${MYVAR}     # Output: "test value" (SAME variable!)
    Log    ${my_var}    # Output: "test value" (SAME variable!)
    Log    ${m y v a r}  # Output: "test value" (SAME variable!)
    
    # These ALL access THE SAME VARIABLE!

Robot Framework normalizes both keywords AND variables. Remember:

  • ✅ Keywords: Case-insensitive and spacing-flexible (Log = log = LOG)
  • ✅ Variables: Case-insensitive and spacing-flexible (${x} = ${X} = ${x_})
  • ✅ Everything is flexible! Robot Framework prioritizes readability

Why Hyphens Aren't Allowed

Robot Framework normalizes keywords by removing spaces and underscores. For example:

  • Log To Console → normalized to logtoconsole
  • Log_To_Console → normalized to logtoconsole

If hyphens were allowed in variables, ${my-var} could be confused with:

  • Subtraction: ${my} - ${var}
  • A keyword with hyphens

So hyphens are reserved for operators, not variable names.

Spaces in Variable Names

Technically valid but rarely used:

*** Test Cases ***
Spaces Example
    ${my variable}    Set Variable    This works!
    Log    ${my variable}
    
    # But most teams prefer underscores:
    ${my_variable}    Set Variable    More readable

Why avoid spaces?

  • Less readable in complex expressions
  • Harder to distinguish from keywords
  • Not common in programming (breaks conventions)

Best Practices

ContextStyleExample
Local variables Snake case ${user_name}, ${api_key}
Constants (*** Variables *** section) All caps ${API_URL}, ${MAX_RETRIES}
Arguments Snake case ${input_file}, ${expected_result}
Loop variables Short, descriptive ${item}, ${user}, ${i}

Consistency is Key

Pick a style and stick to it throughout your test suite:

  • ✅ Good: All snake_case throughout
  • ❌ Bad: Mix of ${userName}, ${user_name}, ${UserName}

Real-World Example

*** Variables ***
${API_URL}         https://api.example.com    # Constant: all caps
${MAX_TIMEOUT}     30s                        # Constant: all caps

*** Test Cases ***
User Login Test
    ${username}        Set Variable    testuser@example.com    # Local: snake_case
    ${password}        Set Variable    SecurePass123           # Local: snake_case
    ${response}        POST    ${API_URL}/login               # Uses constant
    ${status_code}     Set Variable    ${response.status}      # Local: snake_case
    Should Be Equal    ${status_code}    200

MENTOR-9: "Create variables using different naming styles. Then demonstrate flexibility by creating ${test} and accessing it as ${TEST}. Show me you understand Robot Framework's forgiving nature."
